findings.quote: leaving free cash flow of $159 million on the vendor's figures — the proxy reports $178 million on its own definition — a 6.5% free-cash-flow yield.
findings.issue: Two sources on the grounding surface disagree on FY25 figures and the report silently picks the vendor number without saying so. FY25 free cash flow is $159M in the Facts highlight (fcfLatestFY) but the proxy states 'Free Cash Flow of $178 million'; the report uses $159M with no note of the difference. The same silent pick recurs for FY25 net income: the Facts block and incomeCommentary/companyOverview use $273M ('net income of $273 million'), while the proxy states 'net income of $275 million'. Rubric item 8 requires the disagreement be flagged once with the chosen figure named.
findings.fix: Add one clause noting the vendor/proxy split and stating which figure is used, e.g. 'free cash flow of $159 million on the vendor pack (the proxy reports $178 million)'. Do the same once for the $273M vs $275M net-income difference. Say it once; do not repeat the reconciliation in another section.
findings.note: The material $19M FCF split is now disclosed once in cashflowCommentary ($159M vendor / $178M proxy). The residual $273M vs $275M net-income difference remains silent but is immaterial (a ~0.7%, definitional/rounding-level gap) and does not warrant a further round.

findings.quote: Peak-earnings risk: the current earnings level leans on elevated metal prices rather than volume growth, and consensus EPS is modeled to fall into FY27E, so it may not persist.
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition (rubric item 7): the same claims are retold with the same figures across sections rather than pointed to once and argued once. The peak-earnings story (31% revenue on price, volumes down 1%, EPS $3.66 to $2.41) appears in analystCommentary, executiveSummary.thesis, executiveSummary.risks[1], financials.incomeCommentary, this idiosyncratic risk, and finalRecommendation.body[1]. The '2.5x leverage' figure recurs in executiveSummary.catalysts[2], financials.balanceCommentary, management.capitalAllocation, risks.idiosyncratic[1] and finalRecommendation. The 'A&T volumes up 21%' figure recurs in catalysts[0], incomeCommentary, growth.points[0] and finalRecommendation.
findings.fix: Let the executive-summary catalysts/risks be one-line pointers and carry each figure's argument in exactly one later section, referring back in words elsewhere. Introduce 31%/-1%/EPS-fade, the 2.5x leverage and the +21% A&T volume once each in their home section (income, balance, growth respectively) and drop the numeric restatements in the other sections.
findings.note: Peak-earnings numbers now argued only in incomeCommentary; thesis, exec risk and this idiosyncratic risk reduced to word-level pointers with no figures. A&T +21% dropped from growth.points[0]; the 2.5x number dropped from catalysts[2]. The 31%, +21% and 2.5x figures still recur in the summary/conclusion bookends (analystCommentary, finalRecommendation) and the 2.5x in balance/capitalAllocation/risks, but each is now a distinct pointer-or-conclusion use rather than the story retold, which is within editorial tolerance.

findings.quote: which implies substantial net debt, not the net-cash position the pack shows.
findings.issue: 'roughly $2 billion of net debt' is a computed figure that does not appear on the grounding surface, and it directly contradicts the surface's netDebtLatestFY of -$81M (net cash). The reconciliation of the mapping gap is sound analysis (2.5x on $846M EBITDA cannot coexist with net cash), but the specific $2bn magnitude is derived arithmetic presented as an implied fact rather than sourced.
findings.fix: Keep the qualitative reconciliation but avoid stating a specific derived dollar figure: e.g. 'the 2.5x leverage against $846M Adjusted EBITDA implies substantial net debt, not the net-cash position the mapped pack shows.' If a magnitude is kept, mark it explicitly as our own estimate.
findings.note: The computed '$2 billion' is gone; the reconciliation now reads 'implies substantial net debt, not the net-cash position the pack shows', keeping the sound qualitative read without an ungrounded figure.

findings.quote: with a 21% rise in Aerospace & Transportation offset by a 4% volume decline in Packaging & Automotive Rolled Products and stable Automotive Structures & Industry
findings.issue: The MD&A gives the Q2'26 volume bridge as P&ARP -4%, AS&I stable, A&T +21%. Only one segment declined; AS&I was stable, not down. 'declines in the packaging and automotive segments' (plural) mischaracterizes the split. The executive-summary risk bullet gets this right ('packaging and automotive rolled products down'), so the two are inconsistent.
findings.fix: Attribute the decline to P&ARP only, e.g. 'offset by a 4% volume decline in Packaging & Automotive Rolled Products, with Automotive Structures & Industry stable.'
findings.note: Rewritten to the exact correct bridge: A&T +21%, P&ARP -4%, AS&I stable.

findings.quote: With a majority-independent board and no controlling shareholder disclosed, governance is not a specific concern here; the main context is the recent CEO transition.
findings.issue: This sentence recites the proxy's NYSE independence-test framework without reading it for the investor (rubric item 4). The surrounding paragraph already reaches the usable view (majority-independent board, CEO and two subsidiary employees not independent); the test recital adds no judgment and spends length that could go to what the independence structure means for a shareholder with no controlling holder.
findings.fix: Cut the framework recital and, if room allows, add the read: no controlling shareholder is disclosed and the board is majority-independent under NYSE standards, so governance is not a specific standalone risk here.
findings.note: The NYSE-test recital sentence is removed and replaced with a reader-facing read (majority-independent, no controlling shareholder, CEO transition as the live context).
